newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel sellers seek high prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel sellers seek high prices.

text.p: Gas oil sellers, encouraged by the sustained buying interest from a Singapore trader, has emerged in droves with offers at high levels, traders said on Wednesday.
They noted that sellers were trying to push the high prices, which had been limited to prompt barrels before, to cargoes in the forward weeks in April.
They said traders with arbitrage cargoes were now showing their offers.

The high offer levels seemed to dispel earlier concerns that the arrival of arbitrage cargoes in April --amounting to at least 500,000 tonnes--could force prices down to around $25.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis.

However, traders said the market remained concerned that prices in forward weeks could eventually slip if the local trader, who has so far bought over 3.0 million barrels over the past three weeks, suddenly completed his purchases.
The trader concerned however said he planned to continue buying for the time being.
The trader on Wednesday bid for an April 2-7 lifting cargo at $28.70 per barrel, up 10 cents from Tuesday deals, and at $27.35 for April 13-17.
Three offers were seen ranging between $28.05 and $28.70 per barrel for mid-April lifting fob.

Traders said reports that China was unlikely to import diesel for the second quarter could have sprung from state refiner Sinopec's intention to see domestic prices rise and to avoid buying from the international market which has seen very strong prices lately.

"There are people in China who has tankage and are selling," one trader said. "Sinopec has the oil built they are not selling yet as the (domestic) price is not right for them relative to international prices."
But the trader said Sinopec might be able to get imports to be reduced in the second quarter but not a total stop.

Traders also noted that China was trying its best to buy diesel away from Singapore and has been buying greater volumes from South Korea where premiums were around 40 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes fob basis.
A number of tenders are due to be issued on Thursday, regional trade source said.
Vietnam's Petrolimex is expected to issue its tender for second quarter oil products. Indian Oil Corp also plan to issue its kerosene tender for May delivery.
Nepal is scheduled to issue a tender on March 24-25 to by a cargo each of diesel and kerosene for May delivery. The tender is expected to close on April 1-2, a source in Kathmandu said.
The strong physical diesel market saw April swap values rallying about $1.00 per barrel from Tuesday, while May gained 40 cents.
